name: Aquarium Water Volume Calculator
seoTitle: Aquarium Water Volume Calculator — Formula & Results
seoDesc: Tank capacity is quoted as a nominal volume, but the water you actually hold is less once glass, substrate and decoration are accounted for. Free aquarium wat
summary:
Tank capacity is quoted as a nominal volume, but the water you actually hold is less once glass, substrate and decoration are accounted for. It returns gross volume, true water volume, true volume and weight of the water, and the panel shows all of them at once.

This calculator returns gross and true volume, the weight of the water and the heater and filter turnover the tank needs. Every result is derived from the boxes you fill in, so changing one input updates the whole panel at once. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Aquarium Water Volume
sections.html:
Volume (L) = length × width × height ÷ 1 000; subtract length × width × substrate depth

sections.title: How do I use the Aquarium Water Volume?
sections.html:
The form asks only for what the formula needs — nothing is optional decoration.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: shape set to 1.0, length of 90 cm, width or diameter of 45 cm, water height of 45 cm, substrate depth of 5 cm.

Substituting them into the formula gives gross volume of 182.25 L, true water volume of 162 L, true volume of 42.8 US gal, weight of the water of 162 kg, filter turnover needed (5x per hour) of 810 L/h.

The arithmetic is the page's own: change one box and the result moves by the amount the formula implies, which is the quickest way to convince yourself the tool is honest.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
A raw figure only means something next to the bands it is normally judged against. Here is the scale that goes with this one:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
below 20 LNanovery little buffering; small changes matter
20 – 60 LSmalleasy to maintain, few fish
60 – 200 LCommunitystable, forgiving of mistakes
above 200 LLargestable but heavy: check the floor loading

  • Tanks are sold by external dimensions. A '90 cm' tank usually holds about 90 cm internally, but the glass thickness and the fill line cost another few litres.

  • Water weighs one kilogram per litre, so a 200 L tank is a quarter of a tonne before glass, substrate and cabinet — worth checking against a floor joist span.

  • The old rule of five turnovers per hour suits most freshwater community tanks; marine and cichlid setups want ten or more.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
The arithmetic is simple; the inputs are where things go wrong. The usual culprits:

  • Using external dimensions and filling to the brim in the calculation.
  • Forgetting that substrate and rock displace water, which is most of the error in a heavily decorated tank.
  • Treating US gallons and imperial gallons as the same — they differ by 20%.

faq.q: How many litres is a 90 × 45 × 45 cm tank?
faq.a: 182 L gross, and about 162 L with 5 cm of substrate.

faq.q: How much does a 200 L tank weigh?
faq.a: About 200 kg of water, plus 40–60 kg of glass and stand, plus substrate.

faq.q: What does the Aquarium Water Volume actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns gross volume, true water volume, true volume and weight of the water. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
